earlier_scan.source_named: Jungraithmayr, H. & C. Peust. 2023. La langue kwang et ses dialectes (Republique du Tchad). Full description; not available online.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2024. Emergenz und Genese der Tonalität im Tschadischen. Folia Orientalia 61. doi:10.24425/for.2024.152390
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kwang mentioned only as an 'Alttschadisch' outlier with a marked tonal flip-flop (citing J&P 2023); no word on stress/accent in Kwang.

sources.citation: Newman, Paul. 2022. Comprehensive Bibliography of Chadic and Hausa Linguistics, 5th ed. Bloomington: IUScholarWorks. doi:10.5967/5Q3G-T220
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliography only; Kwang-tagged items: Lukas 1937, Lenssen 1984, Ebert 1987, Pearce 2013a ('Observations concerning the metrical systems of three Chadic languages' -- Kera, Kwang, Zime).

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2024. Review of Jungraithmayr & Peust 2023, La langue kwang et ses dialectes. Folia Orientalia 61: 327-331. doi:10.24425/for.2024.152398
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.328: 'Kwang distinguishes 3 tonal levels (High, Low, Medium)', contour combinations, tonal 'flip-flop' between Southern (Mobu) and Northern (Ngam+Cagin) dialects; nothing on stress/accent. Also states the entire prior Kwang literature = Lukas 1937 wordlist, Lenssen 1984 MA thesis, Ebert 1987.

sources.citation: Guitang, Guillaume. 2024. Review of Jungraithmayr & Peust 2023. Linguistique et Langues Africaines 10(1). doi:10.4000/123px
sources.note: Mentions only tone-scheme inversion between dialects (bàdí Mobu vs bádī Ngam 'father'); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hellmuth, Sam & Mary Pearce. 2020. Prosodic systems: North Africa and the Middle East. Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody ch.12 (AAM, already held).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §12.2.4 Chadic: general remarks (Kera, Migaama, Mawa etc.); Kwang not mentioned.

sources.citation: Peust, Carsten. 2018. The subgrouping of East Chadic. Folia Orientalia 55: 235-253.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kwang lexical/morphological data from Lenssen 1984 and Jungraithmayr's unpublished 1976 lexicon; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pearce, Mary. 2007. The Interaction of Tone with Voicing and Foot Structure: Evidence from Kera Phonetics and Phonology. PhD, University College London (CORE open copy, already held).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kwang named only as Kera's nearest lexical relative (42% cognates) and as a target for future metrical investigation (p.335); no statement on Kwang stress.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Carsten Peust. 2023. La langue kwang et ses dialectes (République du Tchad): Précis de grammaire – Textes – Lexique. AKM 133. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz. ISBN 978-3-447-12141-5; e-book PDF e-ISBN 978-3-447-39491-8 (EUR 48). Need ch.1 'La phonologie' pp.27-37, esp. §1.3 'Le ton' pp.32-37.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked; access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8026.C53 J86 2023); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8026.C53 J86 2023
sources.note: The only full modern description of Kwang; its phonology chapter (tone §1.3) is where any remark on accent/stress or its absence would be; also fixes the dialect (Mobu vs Ngam/Cagin) tone systems. AKM volumes normally become open access on MENAdoc (ULB Halle) after the DMG embargo.

In Henry Tourneux (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics VII: Papers from the 6th BICCL, Villejuif, Sept. 22-23, 2011 (Chadic Linguistics / Linguistique Tchadique / Tschadistik 8), 101-113. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Per Newman 2022 keywords it covers Kera, Kwang and Zime metrical structure -- the single work most likely to state where stress/foot heads fall in Kwang (Pearce analyses Kera as iambic, quantity-sensitive); would supersede anything in J&P 2023 on this point.
